_meta.name: Train Collection — Price Seed Reference
_meta.source: Public auction comps (Stout Auctions, Heritage Auctions, Invaluable listings 2024-2026) + LCCA reference. Ranges are APPROXIMATIONS for ungraded items in good-excellent condition. Boxed/mint examples can sell 2-5x higher. Always verify against current sold-listings before consigning.
_meta.disclaimer: These are guidance numbers, not appraisals. Condition, originality, box, and current market sentiment dominate the actual price. Use AX or a live auction call before selling anything you think is worth >$500.

items.name: Hudson 4-6-4 (1952 only)
items.notes: Single-year run, no Magnetraction. Common despite scarcity — interest is modest.

items.name: Santa Fe F3 AA Set
items.notes: Twin-motor powered + dummy A. Best-running postwar diesel. Sold as a pair.

items.name: Santa Fe F3 AA Set
items.notes: F3 successor to 2333. Sold as a pair.

items.name: GG-1 (1950, green)
items.notes: Rarest postwar GG-1. Single-year, single-set production. Boxed mint can exceed $7,500.

items.name: GG-1 (3-year run)
items.notes: Most common postwar GG-1 due to 3-year production.

items.name: GG-1 (Tuscan or 1962 Black)
items.notes: Tuscan: $600-1800. Black 'Vagell' variant: extraordinary — $10k-$15k+ at Stout. Verify body color + plate.

items.name: Hudson 4-6-4 (scale)
items.notes: Scale Hudson. Two production runs. Late 1960s version is more common but still desirable.

items.name: Steam Locomotive 2-4-2
items.notes: Marx's most common loco. Charming but low value.

items.name: PRR S-2 Turbine Premier
items.notes: Premier-line MTH steam. Value holds well.

items.name: Standard Gauge Loco 4-4-4
items.notes: Iconic prewar Standard Gauge loco. State Set companion.
